name: Village Medieval (Eze Village)
tagline: The perched eagle-nest core, cobbled and car-free
description: The historic hilltop village, all stone lanes and stairs climbing to the Jardin Exotique. Stunning views, artisan shops, and Michelin-recognized restaurants, but tiny, overwhelmed by day-trippers, and short on long-term housing. Best visited for short stays or savored after the tour buses leave in late afternoon.

name: Eze-sur-Mer
tagline: The coastal half, with the train station and beach
description: Down at sea level, this small coastal district has the train station, a rocky beach, and a quieter, more residential feel than the hilltop village. The Nietzsche path climbs from here up to Eze Village. Better suited to daily life than the perched core, with easier access to Nice and Monaco by train.
bestFor: beach access, train commuters, quieter stays
pros: Direct train access to Nice and Monaco
cons: Still a steep climb up to the village

name: Grande Corniche / Col d'Eze area
tagline: The upper ridge road above the village
description: The high Corniche road running along the ridge above Eze, dotted with villas, viewpoints, and hiking access. Feels rural and removed from village crowds, with sweeping panoramas over the whole coast from Nice to Italy. Car-dependent and largely residential, with no real commercial center of its own.
bestFor: villa stays, drivers, hikers seeking solitude

name: Nice (nearby base)
tagline: The practical home base for working remotely near Eze
description: France's fifth-largest city, 8 to 10 km from Eze, with real coworking spaces, a broad remote-work and expat community, more affordable and abundant housing, and an international airport. Most nomads working near Eze actually live in Nice and visit the village as a short train or bus trip.
bestFor: remote work, longer stays, nightlife and community
pros: More housing options and lower costs
cons: Busier and less scenic than Eze
